sentences.text: Shri Nilesh Dave - Advocate for the applicant.
Shri K. K. Tiwari - G.A. for respondent/State.

Order 
1] They are heard and perused the case diary.

2] This is the applicant's third bail application filed under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023/ Section 439 of Cr.P.C. as he is implicated in connection with Crime No.91/2024 registered at Police Station Aambua, District- Alirajpur (MP) for offence punishable under Sections 366, 376(2)(N), 343 and 506(Part-2) of IPC.
The applicant is in custody since 28.04.2024.

His first bail application M.Cr.C. No.26261 of 2024 was dismissed by this Court on 08.07.2024 as withdrawn with liberty to renew the prayer after the prosecutrix is examined in the trial Court, whereas his second bail application M.Cr.C. No.774 of 2025 was dismissed on merits vide order dated 13.03.2025.

3] Counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant is lodged in jail since 28.04.2024, and there is no apprehension that he would temper with the evidence, as the prosecutrix has already been examined, and there are material omissions and contradictions in her statement, and,
admittedly, she has resided with the applicant for around 8 days, and during this time, she was photographed along with applicant.
Thus, it is prayed that the application be allowed.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17344 2 MCRC-28165-2025 4] Counsel for the State has opposed the prayer.

Ritesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136897488/
1 5] Having considered the rival submissions, perusal of the case-diary, and taking note of the fact that the prosecutrix has already been examined, and the applicant is lodged in jail since 28.04.2024,
and the final conclusion of trial is likely to take sufficient long time, this Court is inclined to allow the present application.

sentences.text: 6] Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application filed by the applicant is hereby allowed.

The applicant is directed to be released on bail upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (rupees twenty five thousand) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his/her regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he / she shall remain present before the court concerned during trial and shall also abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 437 (3) Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.
7] Accordingly, the application is allowed and disposed of.

(SUBODH ABHYANKAR) JUDGE Pankaj Ritesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136897488/
